newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER AFTER T-BILL TENDER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER AFTER T-BILL TENDER.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market softened on Friday after a drop in the benchmark treasury bill rate at Thursday's weekly auction, dealers said.
"The market is very liquid at the moment and today we are expecting maturities worth Z$1.3 billion," one dealer said.

He said discount houses were now purchasing central bank paper at a lower rate at 20.21 percent from last week's 21.46 percent and selling them in the market at 19.5 percent, down from Thursday's 20.50 percent.
NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold at 22 and 20 percent respectively, down from 23 and 22 percent.
Bankers acceptance rates slid to 20.50 and 19.50 percent from their previous 21.50 and 21 percent while call money shed two percentage points to 20 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated a market surplus at opening of Z$342 million from Z$582 million on Thursday.
